transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alan Reyes (Heritage CTO), Priya Nair (Head of Compliance), Tommy Lee (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, i have Maya, our systems engineer, with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alan: Good thanks, big agenda today, Priya's got a list of compliance Qs.
[00:10] Priya: yep, we just want to make sure any LLM workload meets our bank controls, mainly data residency, audit logs, and retention.
[00:18] Maya: great, we can walk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and the controls around logging, k m s, and SSO. just to ground: are you primarily evaluating for customer support and internal search POCs? or broader use?
[00:30] Alan: starts with customer support & search, but roadmap includes internal docs with customer PII so it's sensitive. can you do EU-only storage? we have branches in EU and US.
[00:40] Maya: yes, for Private and Dedicated we can pin workloads to regions and control residency. Hosted API by default stores telemetry in US, but we offer contractual controls and limited processing options — though for strict EU-only residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:54] Priya: does Redwood have a data processing addendum for GDPR? and do you process logs that might contain PII?
[01:03] Jordan: we have a DPA and standard SCCs; i'll send the legal pack. as for logs, default retention is 30 days for traces and tokens in Hosted but we offer redaction options and can disable request/response logging in Private.
[01:20] Priya: disabled logging is important. for audits we also need tamper-evident audit logs, retention policy controls and ability to export to our SIEM.
[01:29] Maya: Private supports streaming audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding, and we integrate with common syslog/secure endpoints. Dedicated can also forward but there are nuances with managed services. we support sending logs to customer-owned storage with encryption in transit.
[01:45] Tommy: what's the KMS story? we need keys in our control for any customer data at rest.
[01:50] Maya: we support customer-managed KMS for Private (bring your own KMS/HSM). Dedicated can be configured to use KMS in your cloud account for encryption of cached artifacts; Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but enterprise contracts can include BYOK options with HSM in specific regions.
[02:05] Alan: ok. what about HIPAA, we have some teams that might touch protected health info for certain products.
[02:11] Jordan: we have customers in healthcare; we can sign BAA for private deployments and Dedicated depending on contract. we'll share the HIPAA/BAA language.
[02:19] Priya: SOC2 Type II? can you share the report?
[02:22] Jordan: yes, i'll send SOC2 Type II and our ISO summary as a follow up.
[02:27] Tommy: network topology — if we go Private on-prem or VPC, do you require a dedicated peering or can it be via VPN? what about egress?
[02:36] Maya: options: VPC peering, private link, or site-to-site VPN. for on-prem air-gapped we offer an appliance with sync windows. egress is controlled by your routing; we can restrict outbound only to specific Redwood control plane endpoints for updates, and in Private mode the control plane can be in your network.
[02:52] Alan: latency/cost tradeoffs — Dedicated solves latency for high throughput but costs more; Hosted is cheapest but data residency is hard. is there a middle ground?
[03:02] Maya: yes, Dedicated in a region with reserved capacity is a balance. you can also use regional Dedicated pools for EU-only workloads. caching and prefix caching reduce tokens and cost.
[03:12] Priya: about logging retention — bank policy is 7 years for certain audit trails. can logs be archived that long? and filtered to remove PII?
[03:22] Maya: we can stream and archive logs to your S3 (or equivalent) for long term retention, and we support redaction pipelines to strip PII before storage. note: in Hosted we cannot promise 7 years for raw request bodies unless contractually scoped.
[03:40] Tommy: are there any limits on removing training data from model weights, like right to be forgotten?
[03:46] Jordan: models are not retrained on customer data by default in Hosted; we don't incorporate customer prompts into model training. for Private deployments, models run in your environment so training is your responsibility. we can also enable prompt-level redaction at the edge.
[04:01] Priya: auditability — we need a clear mapping of user -> request -> model version and hash. can you surface that in logs?
[04:08] Maya: yes, logs include request id, model id, and model version. we can include KV cache hit/miss metadata but we often mask token-level content. model hashes and container image ids can be included for attestation.
[04:21] Alan: any certifications for data residency in EU? do you support data centres in frankfurt or dublin?
[04:27] Jordan: yes, Dedicated and Private can be deployed in EU regions like frankfurt, dublin. Hosted availability depends on our regional rollout; i'll clarify current region coverage.
[04:40] Priya: about SSO and RBAC — we require SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and granular roles.
[04:47] Maya: supported. Redwood supports SAML, OIDC, SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC. for Private we can also integrate with your LDAP.
[04:58] Tommy: on the security docs, please include network ports required, CA certs, and whether we need to open 443 only.
[05:04] Maya: typically outbound 443 to control plane endpoints, and inbound only for admin consoles if you choose to expose them; we'll provide exact CIDR ranges.
[05:15] Jordan: timeline question — if we choose Dedicated pilot, what's the typical lead time?
[05:20] Maya: for Dedicated reserved capacity in a new region, plan 4–6 weeks for provisioning and validation. Private on-prem or VPC has more variability, typically 6–10 weeks depending on network approvals.
[05:33] Priya: can we get a canary/policy for fallback — if a region is down can requests failover to another region? but for residency we need strict controls.
[05:42] Maya: we support routing policies: strict residency (no failover outside region) or preferential failover (allow to failover to a defined region). we'll surface those in the rollout config.
[05:55] Alan: curious about tokenization and embeddings storage. do you store embeddings persistently?
[06:01] Maya: embedding indices can be stored in your cluster or in Redwood-managed stores; for residency reasons we recommend storing embedding indices in your VPC or Private deployment.
[06:10] Jordan: quick note on pricing — Dedicated is commit-based, lower unit cost; Private has platform fee + support. i'll provide a pricing comparison.
[06:18] Priya: the compliance team will need a contact for on-call incident reporting and data breach timelines.
[06:24] Jordan: we'll provide a support SLA contact and escalation matrix.
[06:27] Tommy: performance benchmarks — we need to run 95th percentile latency tests with our request distribution. can we run a benchmark against a Dedicated instance?
[06:33] Maya: yes, we can provision a short-lived Dedicated test pool or run a Private trial; we'll coordinate sample traffic patterns and metrics.
[06:40] Alan: any blockers for us starting a pilot? approvals we need internally?
[06:44] Priya: legal wants to review DPA, SOC2, and BAA if HIPAA is in scope. infra wants network details and a small PoC.
[06:54] Jordan: that's reasonable. action items: i'll send security docs and pricing, Maya will send network diagram and we'll schedule the perf call.
[07:03] Priya: one more — can you redact sensitive tokens from logs automatically?
[07:08] Maya: yes, we support automatic token redaction and configurable field-level scrubbing. in Private you can push redaction rules.
[07:18] Alan: do you have any clients in banking we can reference?
[07:22] Jordan: yes, several regional banks — i'll share anonymized references and case studies.
[07:28] Tommy: technical note: we use strict egress filtering and only allow certain FQDNs; need to confirm those.
[07:35] Maya: understood, we'll provide exact hostnames and cert pins if needed.
[07:40] Jordan: open question for Maya — is there anything else from a security posture perspective?
[07:44] Maya: just that we recommend Dedicated in-region for initial pilot if residency is a hard requirement; Private if you need full control. also we'll validate key rotations and HSM integrations during the PoC.
[07:58] Alan: ok sounds good. let's talk timeline — target for pilot kickoff in mid April.
[08:03] Jordan: noted. we'll aim to have docs and pricing early next week.

[08:10] --- End of recorded transcript (the rest of the meeting included some overlapping chatter and a short demo link share) ---

Notes about transcript quality: automatic transcript had a few mis-transcribed acronyms (KMS sometimes as K-M-S, VPC as V-P-C), occasional speaker attribution noise. references shared: link to Redwood security whitepaper (sent by Jordan), sample DPA doc, and a placeholder for SOC2 report.

Recap / Next Steps (verbatim from meeting):
- Jordan to send SOC2 Type II + ISO summary + DPA and BAA language where applicable.
- Maya to share Private deployment topology diagram and example KMS/HSM flow.
- Schedule technical deep dive with Tommy to run Dedicated benchmark (95p latency) and confirm peering/VPN requirements.
- Jordan to provide pricing comparison for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and commit options for Dedicated pilot.

Action items captured above.
